audit.why: Chart reads Skill, Skill, Locke, Locke, Locke, Locke, Locke in both layers and matches the packet exactly; every why describes its own row, and 47.44% over 782 games supports a lane that starts even and slides.
audit.corrected: No chart edits. Rows 0-1 Skill, rows 2-6 Locke, full and content already agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] carried only 3 entries where 4 are expected, so the reader lost a whole spike row; and Ashen Pursuit's cooldown appeared only as the vague 'ten seconds of nothing'.
audit.why: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank and is his only mobility — that is the single most actionable number in the matchup, and it deserves the missing spike slot.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] created (before: null) around the flat 10s post-E window; the 10s stated in whys[3] and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Purgatory GROUNDS. The page repeatedly tells you All Out is bad because it strips resistances, and never mentions that the ult also shuts off the W, E and R dashes you would use to reach him or leave the zone. Also two naming problems — the Q is called 'Ritual Nails' throughout when the kit text names Soul Nails, and 'Silver Stake' in whys[0]/early is not an ability Locke has at all.
audit.why: Kit text is the authority. Grounding is the difference between 'All Out is a bad trade' and 'All Out physically cannot happen inside his ult'.
audit.corrected: Grounding written into the interactions row, whys[4], mid and spikes[1]; Q renamed to Soul Nails; 'Silver Stake' removed; Soul Ignition named for the self-damage-and-refund trade with its true damage stated.
sources: kit: Locke R flags grounding + execute

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t states 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source, and Soul Ignition's end-of-duration refund is healing. The line talks a reader out of the item that decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Grievous Wounds still applying to the refund. Zhonya's-class answer against the execute left in place — that part was right.

edits.before: Locke wins by landing Ritual Nails (Marks), stacking you to 2-3, and cashing the blink-bite — then Purgatory forecloses any fight you keep taking at low HP.
edits.after: Locke wins by landing Soul Nails, stacking you to 2-3, and cashing the blink-bite — then Purgatory grounds and executes any fight you keep taking at low HP.

edits.before: Soak the tax, punish the spent blink, and make the execute floor irrelevant by never fighting under it. Track Ritual Nails before every commit and watch your own mark count like a cooldown.
edits.after: Soak the tax, punish the spent blink, and make the execute floor irrelevant by never fighting under it. Track Soul Nails before every commit and watch your own mark count like a cooldown.

edits.before: Track Locke’s Ritual Nails (Marks): The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Commit only while it is down.
edits.after: Track Locke’s Soul Nails: the marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents. Purgatory also GROUNDS: it shuts off your W, E and R dashes, so never save them for inside the zone.

edits.before: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Locke Soul Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — the marks are his whole engine; without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents, so sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): a flat 10s and his ONLY mobility — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): it grounds your dashes, so never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Grievous Wounds still applies — Soul Ignition's refund is a heal.

edits.before: His Silver Stake and Ritual Nails punish your huge HP bar while your level-1 damage is nil.
edits.after: Soul Nails marks punish your huge HP bar from 950 range while your level-1 damage is nil.

edits.before: His grey-health W trades erode you faster than you can sustain at level 3.
edits.after: Soul Ignition's true damage refunds to him, eroding you faster than you sustain.

edits.before: Through 4-5 he out-DPSes your tankiness and dodges your pull-stun with his dash.
edits.after: Through 4-5 he out-DPSes your tankiness and dodges the pull with Ashen Pursuit (10s).

edits.before: His Purgatory ignores effective HP and punishes the resistances you strip in All Out.
edits.after: Purgatory executes through effective HP and grounds the dash All Out relies on to reach him.

edits.before: His percent-execute scaling means your HP stacking never lets you escape him late.
edits.after: His execute scales with every seal, so HP stacking never lifts you above his floor late.

edits.before: Purgatory ignores effective HP — and All Out's stripped resistances make you MORE killable, not less.
edits.after: Purgatory executes through effective HP and grounds your dashes — All Out's stripped resists make it worse.
Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s and his only exit — the ten seconds after he spends it is the entire window you get to step up and commit in.

edits.before: Call it what it is: a counter-pick. His Silver Stake and Ritual Nails tax your HP bar in percentages while your level-1 damage is nil, and his grey-health trades erode you faster than you sustain. Trade as little as possible, hold W to interrupt his dash-in, and treat safe CS under tower as success.
edits.after: Call it what it is: a counter-pick. Soul Nails marks tax you from 950 range while your level-1 damage is nil, and Soul Ignition's true damage refunds straight back to him, eroding you faster than you sustain. Trade as little as possible, hold W for his Ashen Pursuit dash-in, and treat safe CS under tower as success.

edits.before: It gets no better at 6 — Purgatory ignores effective HP, and All Out actively helps him by stripping the resistances you rely on. Never transform just to duel him. Use Q and W to survive his engages, keep the wave close to your tower, and pull jungle or lane-swap pressure toward this lane.
edits.after: It gets no better at 6 — Purgatory executes through effective HP AND grounds you, so the All Out dash meant to reach him simply stops. Never transform just to duel him. Use Q and W to survive his engages, keep the wave close to your tower, and pull jungle pressure toward this lane.

notes: TWO things I could not verify and did not touch. (1) 'Silver Stake' appears in whys[0] and early as one of Locke's abilities — there is no such ability in his kit file (P unnamed on-hit, Q Soul Nails, W Soul Ignition, E Ashen Pursuit, R Purgatory). I removed it rather than keep a name I cannot source, but if it is a real passive/item name the user knows, whys[0] should be revisited. (2) '125 range' for Locke appears in three full-layer strings; his kit lists no basic-attack range, so I left every instance alone. suspectNames flagged "All Out's" — FALSE POSITIVE, correct possessive. spikes[3] was genuinely absent (packet defect confirms 3 of 4) and was created with before:null rather than left as a visible gap.
